title: Realistic Feistel Plaintext-Recovery Thresholds
summary: Plaintext-recovery attacks cover idealized low-round Feistel-type designs, but exact feasible-versus-provably-impossible round thresholds for realistic instantiations remain open.

formal_statement.body: Realistic instantiations of Feistel-type block-cipher designs may differ from idealized low-round settings: practical deployments typically use significantly more rounds, and their round functions need not be ideal random functions. Characterize the exact round thresholds under such realistic instantiations at which full plaintext recovery becomes feasible or, conversely, can be provably ruled out.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of realistic Feistel-type block-cipher designs with more rounds and potentially nonideal round functions.
parameters: Number of rounds — determines the sought thresholds for feasible or provably excluded full plaintext recovery
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the exact round thresholds at which full plaintext recovery becomes feasible or can be provably ruled out for realistic instantiations.

citations.label: Classical and Quantum Full Plaintext Recovery for Low-Round Feistel-Type Designs

progress.summary: The paper contrasts its attacks on idealized low-round structures with practical deployments using more rounds and potentially nonideal round functions. It explicitly presents determination of the exact recovery thresholds for realistic instantiations as open.
citation_labels: Tingting Guo et al., Classical and Quantum Full Plaintext Recovery for Low-Round Feistel-Type Designs
